topics.topic: Exact HTTP refusal contract for malformed placement requests and invalid project IDs
questions: What HTTP status and refusal code/body must be returned for an absent or malformed body, an extra field, a non-list `source_ids`, a list outside the size range, a non-string item, and an invalid project UUID?

What exact refusal answer, error code and HTTP status apply separately to malformed JSON, a non-object body, an extra field, a missing `source_ids`, a non-list value, a list outside 1 to 50 items, a non-string item and an invalid project id?
What exact status, error code and response body are returned for each request-form defect and for an invalid project id?

quotes:
A call holds from 1 to 50 source ids, otherwise it is refused whole. Checks run in this order:
   token, request form and project id, connection, photo folder, every source id. The request form is
   a body holding only `source_ids`, a list of 1 to 50 strings; a defect of that form or of the project
   id is refused before the clock is read.
judgement.why: The placement request-form passage is unchanged from the text with which State 2 was closed, and no subsequent State 2 change made its HTTP-contract detail newly material.

topics.topic: Accepted project UUID representations and canonicalization rules
questions: Which textual UUID representations are accepted: only canonical hyphenated lowercase UUIDs, canonical UUIDs in either case, or every representation accepted by the UUID parser, and are any UUID versions or the nil UUID excluded?
Which textual UUID representations are accepted, and is every accepted value canonicalized before connection lookup, locking and construction of stored paths?

quotes:
A project id must be a UUID and a source id 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Neither a file
   name nor any other received text becomes part of a stored path.
judgement.why: The UUID-form passage is unchanged from the text with which State 2 was closed, and no subsequent State 2 change made the representation question matter.

topics.topic: Authoritative source-ID policy location and named refusal-code enumeration member
questions: The refusal code must become a named member of a models enumeration and the passage must name that member beside the enumeration address.
The passage must place the source-id format policy in its one permitted value domain and place the closed refusal code in a models enumeration, with the later note using the required path form.

quotes:
A string that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters is
   a malformed source id, and one malformed source
   id refuses the whole call with `invalid_source_id` before anything is written.
judgement.why: The source-id and refusal-code passage is unchanged from the text with which State 2 was closed, and the reopening introduced no change that made its value path newly relevant.

topics.topic: Authoritative value domain and code path for placement request limits and field policy
questions: The passage must name the list-size threshold through its single code path, normally as an imported provider constant, instead of leaving the generated code to obtain the literal policy value from prose.
The passage must assign the cardinality limits and request-field policy to their single permitted value domain and state the corresponding path by which generated code receives them.

quotes: A call holds from 1 to 50 source ids, otherwise it is refused whole.

The request form is
   a body holding only `source_ids`, a list of 1 to 50 strings; a defect of that form or of the project
   id is refused before the clock is read.
judgement.why: The placement cardinality and request-field passages are unchanged from the closed State 2 text, and no subsequent State 2 change made their value-domain question newly material.

topics.topic: Calls and refusal paths required to test the at-most-once clock-read invariant
questions: Which refusal and replay paths must be exercised to demonstrate the invariant that every operation reads the clock at most once, including zero-read early refusals and one-read later refusals?

Which successful and refused calls must this test exercise, since A3 and A7 require zero readings for request-form and project-id refusals, one reading before source-id validation, and at most one reading for later refusals?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about INV-13 coverage of pre-clock refusals, post-clock branches and replays that P1 already judged.

precedent.topic: Define INV-13 clock-read tests for pre-clock refusals, post-clock branches, and replays
quotes:
A request refused before that point and the health answer do not read it. A request
   refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing.

- INV-13: a counting clock is read exactly once by each of scan, placement and mark and not at all by the health answer (`test_each_operation_reads_the_clock_once`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
precedent.why: The clock-test wording and the pre-clock, post-clock and replay clauses are unchanged from the closed text, and the inserted placement-source-id sentence did not create this test-coverage question.

topics.topic: How tests prove that no scanning occurs for unusable connections
questions: What must the Required tests show to prove INV-10's claim that nothing is scanned when the connection is missing, invalid or unconfirmed, rather than merely showing the answer and absence of writes?
How must the test demonstrate the invariant's claim that nothing is scanned, rather than merely checking the final refusal and durable writes?

quotes: - INV-10: nothing is scanned, placed or marked for a project unless the connections file read by that operation is valid and holds a confirmed connection for the project.

- INV-10: scan, placement and mark each answer `connection_not_confirmed` for an unconfirmed connection (`test_an_unconfirmed_connection_delivers_nothing`). After a scan has succeeded on the running service, clearing the confirmation makes scan, placement and mark each answer `connection_not_confirmed` and write nothing (`test_a_cleared_confirmation_stops_the_running_service`). For a valid file with no record for the project, scan, placement and mark each answer `unknown_project` and write nothing (`test_a_project_without_a_connection_delivers_nothing`). For an absent file, a file that cannot be opened, a file that is not UTF-8 or JSON, a file of another form and a record that breaks the form of rule 8, also when that record is unconfirmed or belongs to another project, scan, placement and mark each answer `folder_unavailable` and write nothing (`test_unreadable_connections_deliver_nothing`), and the service does not start (`test_the_service_does_not_start_with_an_unreadable_connection_record`).
judgement.why: Both the invariant and its Required tests wording are unchanged from the closed State 2 text, and the reopening did not make this test-evidence question newly material.

topics.topic: Precedence between request-form and project-ID validation failures
questions: Within the combined “request form and project id” stage, which check wins when both are invalid?
Within the combined “request form and project id” step, which check takes precedence when both are invalid?

quotes:
Checks run in this order:
   token, request form and project id, connection, photo folder, every source id.
judgement.why: The combined request-form and project-id validation stage is unchanged from the closed State 2 text, and no later State 2 change introduced or affected the precedence question.

topics.topic: Treatment and testing of connection subfolders that resolve outside their root
questions: What exactly must `A connection leaving its root is not loaded` test, given that rule 8 expressly forbids resolved-path checking at startup and for records belonging to other projects: only the requested project's photo folder during scan or placement, every record while loading, or some different root-boundary check?
May the deliverer load and use a confirmed ObjectConnection whose syntactically valid invoice subfolder resolves outside the root, or must that record be rejected to preserve M01?
Does “a connection leaving its root” cover the resolved invoice subfolder, or only syntactically escaping paths and the requested photo folder?

quotes: Both subfolders stay inside the root.

The form of a subfolder: the photo and invoice subfolders are non-empty relative paths without
   `..` and are not the root itself. Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`. This second check does not run at
   the start of the service or for other projects. The deliverer never opens the invoice folder, so
   the resolved path of that folder is checked by the Cabinet Inbox when it moves to this record
   (R0-09).

A connection leaving its root is not loaded (`test_a_connection_cannot_leave_the_object_root`), and a linked folder outside the root is refused (`test_a_photo_folder_linked_out_of_the_root_is_refused`).
judgement.why: The model assertion, deferred invoice-folder check and Required tests wording all appear unchanged in the closed texts, and no State 2 change made their relationship newly material.

provenance.quote: Both subfolders stay inside the root.

topics.topic: Valid subfolder path grammar, separators, and normalization
questions: Does “without `..`” prohibit the literal substring anywhere or only a path component equal to `..`, and which separators and normalized spellings such as `.`, `./photos`, repeated separators and backslashes satisfy the form?

What exact path grammar and normalization define a valid subfolder, including whether `..` means a path component or any substring, whether `.` components are allowed, how separators are treated, and when equivalence to the root is tested?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about relative-subfolder grammar, separators and normalization that P8 assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Define lexical path rules for relative subfolders, parent components, separators, and normalization
precedent.why: The authoritative path grammar, separators, normalization, forbidden components, and accepted textual forms are contract and format details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Exact serialized representation of clock instants
questions: What exact serialized representation is required, including the date-time separator, whether six fractional digits are always present, and whether a UTC suffix is forbidden or required?

topics.topic: HTTP status, response shape, and detail for malformed source-ID refusals
questions: Is `invalid_source_id` an HTTP-level refusal or a placement response, what HTTP status and response shape does it use, and does it identify the offending list position or value?

topics.topic: Placement validation failures that occur before versus after the clock read
questions: Is a malformed placement source id checked before or after the operation reads the clock?
Which fields of scan, placement and mark are “path identifiers,” and therefore which invalid project, source and photo identifiers are rejected before the clock is read?

quotes:
A string that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters is
   a malformed source id, and one malformed source
   id refuses the whole call with `invalid_source_id` before anything is written.

Scan, placement and mark each read it once, after the token, the request form and the path
   identifiers are accepted and before the project lock is taken or any connection, file or record is
   examined. A source id in the body of a placement is not a path identifier: it is checked after the
   clock, at the place A3 rule 4 gives it.
judgement.why: The source-id refusal and clock-order passages are unchanged from the closed State 2 text, and the reopening introduced no change that affected their validation-order question.
